subject: Pricing & caching assumptions — post-call recap
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@fastretail.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@fastretail.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Pricing & caching assumptions — post-call recap

Thanks again for the time today — quick post-call recap and next steps so we stay aligned. TL;DR: key inputs we discussed (token volumes, budget target) + caching assumptions materially change the effective $/1M.

Call highlights:
- Target account: FastRetail — serviced conversational agents and product Q&A.
- Confirmed rough monthly token scenarios: low ~50M, typical ~120M, peak ~350M.
- Current target budget (as discussed): mid-range (~$10k–$15k/month) — clarifying that this is for inference only.
- Typical prompt/response: avg prompt ~25–40 tokens, avg response ~60–120 tokens.

Caching assumptions I recommended:
- Prefix / KV caching (agent prompts + product context) looks promising given high repetition in salutations and product-lookup prompts.
- Estimated cacheable traffic: 35%–50% (we used 45% as a working assumption on the call).
- Average cacheable prefix length: ~25–35 tokens — we cache prefixes and avoid re-generating common context.
- Expected hit-rate sensitivity: if user flows are templated (forms, same product IDs) hit rate moves toward 50%+, if free-form queries it may be closer to 30%–35%.

Unit economics examples (model list price = $35 per 1M tokens — illustrative):
- No cache: $35/1M -> for 120M tokens = 120 * $35 = $4,200
- 40% cache hit: billable tokens = 120M * (1 - 0.4) = 72M -> 72 * $35 = $2,520 (effective $/1M billed = $2,520 / 72 = $35, but effective per-original-1M = $2,520 / 120 = $21)
- 60% cache hit -> billable 48M -> cost = 48 * $35 = $1,680 -> effective per-original-1M = $14

Notes on pricing interpretation: in the examples above, "effective $/1M tokens" refers to the cost normalized to the original incoming token volume (i.e., how much you pay per 1M of user tokens after cache savings). The base model price and caching behavior both drive this metric.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Olivia/Samir: please send the usage snapshot (hourly traffic shape & a few sample transcripts) — I flagged an attachment name below for easy upload.
2) Redwood (Marcus/Aditya + me): we'll produce a short estimate PDF with: a) 3 pricing scenarios (no-cache / 40% hit / 60% hit), b) recommended cache config (prefix length, TTLs), and c) breakouts for burst months.
3) Schedule a 30m follow-up to walk the estimate & pick a path (self-serve trial vs. pilot with a small committed band). I suggest Thu Jan 21 or Fri Jan 22.

Attachments: we typically use a usage snapshot + short pricing sheet. For now, please upload a CSV/XLS with hourly usage if possible (example filename: FR_USAGE_SNAPSHOT.xlsx).

Thanks — happy to run the numbers for any alternate hit-rate you want to see.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

- Our internal budget for inference-only is ~ $12k / month to start (we can expand after we see unit economics).

Can you show the 120M example side-by-side with the cache hit assumptions? Specifically: if we target 40% hit, what does that mean against our $12k budget? Also want to understand how burst months would affect billing and whether there are smoothing/committed options.

I'm available for a 30m follow-up on Fri Jan 22 (10am PT or 2pm PT).

Olivia / Samir — appreciated. Attached is the short estimate PDF I promised (redwood-pricing-estimate.pdf) with three scenarios and a simple calc table. Quick numbers inline for the 120M case you asked about: 

- Base model price (illustrative): $35 / 1M tokens -> no-cache cost = 120 * $35 = $4,200
- 40% cache hit -> billable tokens = 72M -> billed cost = 72 * $35 = $2,520 -> effective cost per original 1M = $2,520 / 120 = $21
- 60% cache hit -> billable tokens = 48M -> billed cost = $1,680 -> effective per-original-1M = $14

So with the 40% hit assumption your $12k budget is comfortably above the expected inference spend for 120M at the model price above — this gives room for:
- larger model usage on-demand,
- embedding/feature workloads, or
- expanded SLA/retention add-ons.

Burst months: for the 300–350M spike we recommend either a short-term burst pool (pay-as-you-go) or a small committed band to smooth unit price. The attached PDF includes both a pay-as-you-go and a committed-capacity row (with example discounts at commit levels).

Commits/minimums: no hard minimum for self-serve; pilot/commit discounts are negotiable (we typically structure a 3–6 month pilot commit for enterprise pilots).
